author: DTrim99
body:
Your second thought is exactly right — the age *ceiling* applies only to the income-related version of the deduction, not to the fixed one.

Code of Va. § 58.1-322.03(5) has two separate deductions:

> (a) A deduction in the amount of $12,000 for individuals born **on or before January 1, 1939**.
> (b) A deduction in the amount of $12,000 for individuals born **after January 1, 1939**, who have attained the age of 65. This deduction shall be reduced by $1 for every $1 that [AFAGI] exceeds $50,000 for single taxpayers or $75,000 for married taxpayers.

So your 85-year-old (born 1/1/1937) falls under (a): a flat $12,000 with **no** income test. Your 77-year-old (born 1/1/1945) falls under (b): income-based, and with AFAGI $160,294 well over the $75,000 married threshold it phases to $0. Total = $12,000 — which is what TaxAct allows. The "born between 1939 and 1958" / "$75,000 income limit" language on the worksheet is describing the (b) deduction only; the worksheet even says up top it's for taxpayers "born on or between January 2, 1939, and January 1, 1958."

So TaxAct is right and PE is wrong here: PE lumps both spouses into one combined $24,000 maximum and then subtracts the full income excess from the whole thing, wiping out the 85-year-old's protected $12,000. Filed as PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9302.

(Two notes on the files: the record this describes is in out2psl/**1140**; the directory linked here, 1141, is a different West Virginia return. And I opened the same finding from the VA data that came through on #1139, which had a "MT" title by mistake — closing that one as a duplicate of this.)
